To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the marly rhythmites of the Pliocene (and late Miocene) Trubi Formation in Sicily are a result of alternation of increased dilution by terrigenous material (river runoff) and increased carbonate production in the sea, and that the alternation of these two conditions was probably caused by precessional forcing.

the marly rhythmites of the Trubi Formation of Southern Italy were formed by the alternate predominance in the surface waters of river-supplied siliciclastic material and carbonate-producing microorganisms.

the origin of rhythmic marl-limestone alternations in the Early Plicene of Sicily was due to the alternate predominance, during precession cycles, of increased dilution by river-supplied terriguous material, and decreased carbonate production.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the recognition of the causes of the rhythmic bedding in these Pliocene marls.
the study of the origin and climatic significance of rhythmic alterations of marly and calcareous beds in the Pliocen Trubi Formation of the Sicily Channel, southern Italy.
an attempt to understand the causes of the alternation of carbonate-rich and carbonate-poor beds in the Trubi Formation of southern Italy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the marly rhythmites in the Trubi Formation are not the result of the alternate deposition of terrigenous and biogenic material.
rhythmic alternations of relatively carbonate-pool and relatively carbonate-rich beds in shallow-water sediments of the Mediterranean area are not necessarily of Milankovitch origin.
the Pliocene rhythmic bedding in southern Italy is a consequence of the alternation of relatively humid and relatively arid periods, which are in turn related to the precession of the equinoxes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Pliocene marl-limestone rhythmites of the Trubi Formation of southern Sicily originated from a complex interplay of climate, oceanographic and eustatic changes.
the Trubi Formation of southern Italy is an excellent example of the influence of precession on the sedimentary record.

the rhythmic bedding in these Pliocene marly rhythmites was controlled by the alternation of relatively humid and relatively arid conditions in the catchment area of the rivers and in the surface waters of the adjacent marine basin.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the rhythmicity of the Trubi Formation, which has been considered as the result of the alternation of two different sedimentation processes (i.e. carbonate and terrigenous), is in fact the result of a single sedimentary process (terrigenous) that has been affected by different environmental conditions.
rhythmic bedding can result from a complex interplay of climatic and environmental factors, which can be revealed by a multi-proxy study.
rhythmites are not necessarily the product of the interaction of two end-members (e.g., riverine and marine), but rather of a more complex interaction between different environmental factors.
